points.description: Observes that A_{n+1} − A_n ∈ {0,1} (A_n is slowly increasing, steps of at most 1), and states or proves it as a lemma.

levels.says: Notes A_n is slowly growing or nondecreasing but does not state the 0/1 step property clearly, or states it without justification.

points.description: Sets up a discrete intermediate-value argument: for an integer parameter t (or an equivalent function such as (n+2024)/A_n), defines F(n) = n+2024 − tA_n and notes that F rises only in steps of +1 (or an equivalent step control), so it cannot skip 0 going from negative to nonnegative.

levels.says: Defines the right function or parameter but does not control the steps, or the step claim is wrong or unjustified.

points.description: Shows F is negative at a start (e.g. F(1) = 2025 − t < 0 for t > 2025) and eventually positive. This needs a valid growth bound such as A_n = o(n) (e.g. A_n ≤ √n + n^{1/3}log2 n). Claiming A_n ~ √n without any justification earns only part.

levels.says: Gives only one of the two sign facts, or gives the growth claim without a justification.

points.description: Concludes that some n has F(n) = 0, i.e. n+2024 = tA_n, so A_n | n+2024.
Shows infinitely many distinct n arise, e.g. n ≥ t − 2024 → ∞ as t → ∞, or the n are unbounded for another valid reason.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a complete proof: the 0/1 step property, a discrete intermediate-value argument that hits exactly 0, the growth bound A_n = o(n), and infinitely many distinct n. Part marks are for the step property or a guessed lemma on slow growth, and for an intermediate-value setup that is not completed. A numerical check or a proof that only handles finitely many n earns no marks for the conclusion.
rubric.answer_key:
Let t be an integer with t > 2025. Define F(n) = n + 2024 − t·A_n.
1. A_{n+1} − A_n ∈ {0,1}, because n+1 is either a perfect power or not. So F(n+1) − F(n) = 1 − t(A_{n+1} − A_n) is either +1 or 1−t. Hence F can only go up in steps of exactly +1.
2. F(1) = 1 + 2024 − t = 2025 − t < 0, since A_1 = 1.
3. A_n/n → 0. For each b ≥ 2 there are at most n^{1/b} perfect b-th powers ≤ n, and only b ≤ log2 n matters. So A_n ≤ √n + n^{1/3}·log2 n = o(n). Thus F(n) = n + 2024 − tA_n → +∞, so F(N) > 0 for some N.
4. Let n be the least index with F(n) ≥ 0. Then n > 1 and F(n−1) < 0. Since F(n) ≤ F(n−1) + 1 ≤ 0, we get F(n) = 0. So n + 2024 = t·A_n, and A_n | n + 2024.
5. Infinitely many n: A_n ≤ n gives t = (n+2024)/A_n ≥ (n+2024)/n > 1. This is not enough, so use a sharper bound. From n + 2024 = tA_n and A_n ≤ n we get t ≤ n/A_n + 2024/A_n ≤ n + 2024. So n ≥ t − 2024. As t → ∞, n → ∞, so there are infinitely many distinct n. (Equivalently, each n has only one value of t, and there are infinitely many t.)
Conclusion: infinitely many n satisfy A_n | n + 2024.
